finalText:
Scope: 94 files hit `account_id`. Spans 5 services (accounts, billing, orders, analytics, notify), `lib/`, `vendor/`, 15 migration files, `docs/openapi.yaml`. Big, touch DB column, internal params, service call chains — full day, not small refactor.

**Must NOT rename:**

1. `docs/openapi.yaml` + `lib/serialize.js` — public API field, frozen by contract (comment says so explicit: "keys on RIGHT are public API... an internal rename must not reach this side of the map"). Wire field `account_id` stay `account_id` even if DB column change.
2. `vendor/reporting-sdk/*` — third-party vendored code. Not ours. Rename here just diverge from upstream, break future vendor sync.
3. All `migrations/*.sql` — already applied in production (see `20250624_backfill_account_ids.sql` comment: "Applied migrations are history: editing one does not rename anything in a database that already ran it, and breaks down step"). New rename needs fresh migration, old ones stay untouched.

**Lower-confidence risk:** `lib/audit.js` — log lines keyed `account_id`. If downstream log/alerting pipeline parses by that key name (outside this repo), renaming break it silently. Worth asking platform team before touch.

Safe to rename: internal service/repo/route param names (`account_id` variable through orders/billing/analytics/notify services) — pure internal plumbing, DB column itself (with migration + backfill), as long as wire/API layer stay frozen.

Sign-off line: approve rename of internal column/params, block rename of public API field name, vendor code, and old migration files.
